BURSEVI:v10p332#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p332#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p332#2/r7.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent good deeds ahead for the lasting, useful afterlife, or had performed saving deeds during worldly life; he wants work that keeps him among the living.
BURSEVI:v10p332#2/r7.anchor: يا ليتني عملت لأجل حياتي هذه يعني لتحصيل الحياة الأخروية التي هي حياة نافعة دائمة غير منقطعة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r4.claim: The passage portrays the helplessness of people who loved wealth and failed to turn it into a means of salvation on Judgment Day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r4.anchor: A portrayal of the helplessness and hopelessness on the Day of Judgement of people who remained inebriated with the love of wealth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r3.claim: Those enamored of wealth will recognize their folly and wish they had prepared for the Day, but that regret will be useless when they face the consequences of their deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r3.anchor: all this would prove fruitless for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p313/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p313/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p313/r5.claim: Verse 24 explains the person's realization in verse 23: those who now dismiss warnings will regret failing to prepare for the Hereafter, but the time to amend will have passed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p313/r5.anchor: The time to make amends for it would be long gone.

QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r14.claim: The regret is a wish to have obeyed God and looked after one's own future life.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r1.claim: The statement is either an appositive spelling out what the person remembers, or a reply to an implied question about what he says; the lām can mark purpose or the time of worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r1.anchor: وهذه الجملة بدل اشتمال من يتذكر أو استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r2.claim: One reading is that he wished he had prepared good works for his afterlife; another takes the lām as “during my worldly life,” wishing he had acted then to benefit today. The view that he wished for life is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r2.anchor: والمراد بحياته حياته في الآخرة ومفعول قدمت محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the wish as evidence that a person acts independently; Alusi rejects that inference because the words show perceived capacity, not whether God creates the act or its acquired power.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r3.anchor: وزعمه الزمخشري دليلا على الاستقلال ورد على المجبرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r4.speaker: أهل الحق
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r4.claim: The people of truth do not claim that human choice is wholly removed; a wish may also target the impossible, as with a drowning person, so it does not prove independence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p129/r4.anchor: هذا وأهل الحق لا يقولون بسلب الاختيار بالكلية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423/r1.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent ahead good works and righteous deeds for his eternal afterlife, in which there is no death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423/r1.anchor: {يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} أي قدمت الخير والعمل الصالح لحياتي في الآخرة، أي لآخرتي التي لا موت فيها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r1.claim: The speaker wishes for righteous deeds in this real life or during worldly life; his regret does not prove human acts are independently possible, since the barred can wish an act had been possible.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r1.anchor: { يقول يليتنى قدمت لحياتى } أي لحياتي هذه، أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا أعمالا صالحة

BINTSHATI:v2p158/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the lament as proof that people had choice and were not compelled to obey or sin; the author declines the broader free-will debate.
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r1.anchor: كما حمله الزمخشري في (الكشاف) وإن استطرد فتأوله، على مذهب الإعتزال

BINTSHATI:v2p158/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r2.claim: The speech expresses remorse, including recognition that what has passed cannot return.
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r2.anchor: ونقبل توجيه القول في الآية على التحسر. وفي التحسر معنى الندم والإقرار بأن ما فات هيهات أن يعود.

BINTSHATI:v2p158/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r3.claim: Anna signals distance and layta an impossible or distant wish: the deceived person longs to return and do good before punishment arrives.
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r3.anchor: أنى للبعد، وليت للتمني في البعيد والمستحيل

BINTSHATI:v2p158/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r4.claim: Exegetes differ whether 'my life' means the afterlife, one's former worldly lifetime, or the Quran once denied.
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r4.anchor: واستغنى البيان القرآني عن تحديد "حياتي" فاختلف المفسرون بين أن يكون المراد بها حياتي الآخرة

BINTSHATI:v2p158/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r5.claim: The author prefers the enduring afterlife: worldly life is only a passing journey, and only what one prepares for the next life remains useful.
BINTSHATI:v2p158/r5.anchor: والأولى أن تحمل على الحياة الأخرى الباقية، فما كانت الدنيا سوى رحلة عابرة لحياة فانية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r3.claim: The wish that follows is impossible; the person longs to have sent ahead useful striving and deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r3.anchor: أي متمنيا المحال على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r4.claim: Lihayati can mean for the days of worldly life or for this enduring life in which there is no death; the speaker knows obedience had been possible before.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p422/r4.anchor: أي أيام حياتي في الدنيا أو لأجل حياتي هذه الباقية التي لا موت بعدها

NAHHAS:v5p223/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p223/r13.claim: Some Arabs say laytani, by analogy with anni.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r13.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول ليتي يشبهه بأني

NAHHAS:v5p223/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r14.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p223/r14.claim: He interprets the life for which the person wishes he had prepared as the afterlife.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r14.anchor: قال الضحاك ( قدمت لحياتي ) في الآخرة

NAHHAS:v5p223/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r15.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p223/r15.claim: He says the person realizes there is an endless life beyond this one.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r15.anchor: قال الحسن علم أن ثم حياة لا نفاذ لها

DURR-FULL:v8p512/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r5.claim: He said the person then knows the truth: the afterlife is a long, deathless life better than this one.
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن الحسن رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v8p512/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r6.claim: He glossed ‘my life’ as the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v8p512/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r7.speaker: محمد بن أبي عميرة
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r7.claim: A Companion said that even a lifetime spent obeying God would leave a servant wishing to return to worldly life for more reward.
DURR-FULL:v8p512/r7.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والبخاري في التاريخ والطبراني عن محمد بن أبي عميرة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#3/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#3/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the wish to have sent something ahead for one's life as wishing one had done deeds in this world for the afterlife.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#3/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي يقول : عملت في الدنيا لحياتي في الاخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r2.claim: The first ‘that day’ attaches to ‘brought’; the second replaces the clause about the earth being crushed and is governed with it by ‘remember.’ Fronting stresses the time and builds suspense after a long interruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r2.anchor: و { يومئذ } الأول متعلق بفعل { جيء } . والتقدير : وجيء يوم تدك الأرض دكا دكا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r5.claim: The lament may be spoken aloud, as a circumstantial clause or inclusive substitute for remembering, or be an inward thought explaining the remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r5.anchor: وجملة : { يقول يا ليتني } الخ يجوز أن يكون قولا باللسان تحسرا وتندما فتكون الجملة حالا من { الإنسان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r6.claim: The object of ‘I sent ahead’ is omitted for brevity and means good deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r7.claim: The lām in ‘for my life’ may mean during the first life or for the purpose of attaining a complete life free from punishment, unlike the diminished existence of Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p338/r7.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لحياتي } تحتمل معنى التوقيت ، أي قدمت عند أزمان حياتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p339/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p339/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p339/r1.claim: The vocative particle in the lament draws attention to how momentous this wish will be on the Day it occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p339/r1.anchor: للتنبيه اهتماما بهذا التمني في يوم وقوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r5.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r5.claim: Most interpreters say he wishes he had prepared for his lasting life in the Hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r5.anchor: فقال جمهور المتأولين معناه: لحياتي الباقية يريد في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r6.speaker: قوم من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r6.claim: Some interpret it as life in the grave after resurrection, which the person had denied and thought impossible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r6.anchor: وقال قوم من المتأولين: المعنى لحياتي في قبري عند بعثي الذي كنت أكذب به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r7.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r7.claim: Others read life figuratively: he wishes he had done good works that would give him a good life now.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: لحياتي هنا مجاز، أي ليتني قدمت عملا صالحا لأنعم به اليوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r8.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that he wishes he had prepared for the duration of his past worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين لوقت أو لمدة حياتي الماضية في الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p122/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p122/r1.claim: The speaker longs to have sent righteous deeds ahead in worldly life for the afterlife, where there is no death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p122/r1.anchor: العمل الصالح في الدنيا لحياتي في الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r2.claim: The sinner regrets past disobedience, while even the obedient person wishes he had done more good for the afterlife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r2.anchor: يعني: يندم على ما كان سلف منه من المعاصي -إن كان عاصيا-ويود لو كان ازداد من الطاعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r3.speaker: محمد بن أبي عميرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r3.claim: The Companion Muhammad ibn Abi Umayra says a lifelong worshipper would still consider his service small on Judgment Day and wish to return for more reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r3.anchor: قال: لو أن عبدا خر على وجهه من يوم ولد إلى أن يموت هرما في طاعة الله،

KASHSHAF:89:24/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:24/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:24/r1.claim: For my life may mean the afterlife, or the time of my worldly life, as in dating an event to nights of Rajab; the latter is clearer.
KASHSHAF:89:24/r1.anchor: وهي حياة الآخرة ،   أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا ،   كقولك : جئته لعشر ليال

KASHSHAF:89:24/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:24/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:24/r2.claim: The regret proves people had choice through their intentions and wills and were not prevented from obedience or compelled to sin, as some heretical schools claim.
KASHSHAF:89:24/r2.anchor: وهذا أبين دليل على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r3.claim: Wishing that one had sent something ahead for life means sending provisions from worldly life for the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r3.anchor: أحدهما : قدمت من دنياي لحياتي في الآخرة , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r4.claim: It may mean wishing one had sent something from one's life ahead for the return to the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r4.anchor: الثاني : قدمت من حياتي لمعادي في الآخرة ذكره ابن عباس .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#7/r1.claim: He wishes he had sent righteous deeds ahead during fleeting life for the enduring life of the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#7/r1.anchor: هذه وهى حياة الآخرة أى ياليتنى قدمت الأعمال الصالحة فى الحياة الفانية

QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r1.claim: The phrase may mean 'in my life,' with the preposition li meaning fī.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r1.anchor: أي في حياتي. فاللام بمعنى في.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r2.claim: Alternatively, he wishes he had sent righteous deeds ahead for a life without death.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r2.anchor: وقيل: أي قدمت عملا صالحا لحياتي، أي لحياة لا موت فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r3.claim: Because the Fire's life is miserable, the speaker wishes for good deeds that would save him and grant a pleasant life.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:24/r3.anchor: فالمعنى: يا ليتني قدمت من الخير لنجاتي من النار

QUTB-ZILAL:89:24/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:24/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:24/r1.claim: The afterlife is the true life worthy of that name, and it alone deserved preparation, advance provision, and saving acts; the wish expresses the person’s deepest regret.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:24/r1.anchor: فهي الحياة الحقيقية التي تستحق اسم الحياة . وهي التي تستأهل الاستعداد والتقدمة والادخار لها

RAZI:89:24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:24/r1.claim: One reading has the speaker wish that, during worldly life, he had prepared deeds for the everlasting afterlife; it is called “my life” because true life is there.
RAZI:89:24/r1.anchor: في الدنيا التي كانت حياتي فيها منقطعة ، لحياتي هذه التي هي دائمة غير منقطعة

RAZI:89:24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:24/r2.claim: A second reading says Hell’s people are effectively lifeless despite not dying; the speaker wishes he had done deeds that would save him from Hell and make him among the living.
RAZI:89:24/r2.anchor: فياليتني قدمت عملا يوجب نجاتي من النار حتى أكون من الأحياء

RAZI:89:24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:24/r3.claim: A third reading takes the phrase as wishing he had acted during his lifetime in the world.
RAZI:89:24/r3.anchor: وثالثها : أن يكون المعنى : فياليتني قدمت وقت حياتي في الدنيا

RAZI:89:24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:24/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:89:24/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that people had genuine choice and will and were not prevented from obedience or driven into sin.
RAZI:89:24/r4.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم ومعلقا بقصدهم وإرادتهم

RAZI:89:24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:24/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:24/r5.claim: The author replies that if a person’s intention depends on another intention, the chain regresses infinitely; if it depends on God’s intention, Muʿtazilism is refuted.
RAZI:89:24/r5.anchor: فقصدهم إن كان معلقا بقصد آخر لزم التسلسل ، وإن كان معلقا بقصد الله فقد بطل الاعتزال

ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r6.claim: His “life” is the abode of the Hereafter, where there is no death.
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r6.anchor: أي لدار الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

STUDYQURAN:89:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r2.claim: People will remember their conduct, but can no longer repent or make up lost time.
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r2.anchor: people will remember how they conducted themselves in this world, but there will be no opportunity for repentance

STUDYQURAN:89:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r3.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r3.claim: Most commentators interpret wishing one had sent forth for life as wishing for good deeds that would save one from the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r3.anchor: Most commentators say Would that I had sent forth for my life means, “Would that I had sent forth good deeds

STUDYQURAN:89:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r4.claim: A hadith says believers too will regret each time they remembered God in life, since that remembrance will be a source of regret on Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:89:23/r4.anchor: even believers will have some regret, since as a ḥadīth says, “There is no time wherein the son of Adam does not remember God

TAB:89:24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:24/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:24/r1.claim: The speaker regrets neglecting good deeds in worldly life that would secure enduring afterlife happiness and God's approval.
TAB:89:24/r1.anchor: يا لَيْتَنِي قَدّمْتُ لِحيَاتِي في الدنيا من صالح الأعمال لحياتي هذه ،   التي لا موت بعدها ،   ما ينجيني

TAB:89:24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:24/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB:89:24/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God knows the regret is sincere: the person now faces a long life with no death at its end.
TAB:89:24/r2.anchor: علم الله أنه صادق ،   هناك حياة طويلة لا موت فيها آخر ما عليه

TAB:89:24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:24/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:24/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the lament as recognizing that the afterlife is the truly long life.
TAB:89:24/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  يا لَيْتَنِي قَدّمْتُ لِحَياتِي :  هُناكُم والله الحياة الطويلة

TAB:89:24/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:24/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:89:24/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the life meant as the afterlife.
TAB:89:24/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  يا لَيْتَنِي قَدّمْتُ لِحَياتِي قال :  الاَخرة

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r1.claim: The pairs in verses 15–16 and 29–30 rhyme only approximately through ḏikrā and ḥayātī.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Wie die Verspaare V. 15.16 und V. 29.30 bilden ḏikrā und ḥayātī nur einen näherungsweisen Reim

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r2.claim: Several of the seven canonical readers use imāla for ḏikrā, making it sound closer to ḥayātī than it first appears.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:23-24:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Da ḏikrā jedoch von mehreren der sieben kanonischen Koranlesern mit Imāla gelesen wird, ist die lautliche Nähe zu ḥayātī größer

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:24:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:24:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:24:anmerkung/r1.claim: The commentary directs readers to its note on 82:5 for the verb qaddama.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:24:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu qaddama vgl. die Anmerkung zu 82:5

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Later additions in 23–24 and 27–30 bring the afterlife dimension into the sura and help decode the enigmatic oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Spätere Zusätze (V. 23.24 und V. 27–30) tragen diese eschatologische Dimension dann auch in die vorliegende Sure ein

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.claim: Verses 23–24 and 27–30 are later insertions that expand the original four-verse eschatological unit and enact the oath's duality as an antithesis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 23.24 sind wie V. 27–30 spätere Einschübe (s. o.), die das eschatologische Vierergesätz

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.claim: The inserted clause in 23b–24 focuses on the human response to Hell, paralleling the worldly human responses in the secondary pair 15–16.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.anchor: der vor V. 25.26 eingeschobene zusätzliche eschatologische Nachsatz V. 23b.24 auf den Menschen und seine Reaktion auf die Höllenstrafe fokussiert

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r2.claim: “My life” means the afterlife, the real life, as 29:64 says; what one should have sent ahead is righteous work for it.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r2.anchor: والمراد بالتقديم للحياة تقديم العمل الصالح للحياة الآخرة

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r3.claim: The wish is made when the person remembers the Resurrection and sees that nothing can benefit him.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r3.anchor: وما في الآية تمن يتمناه الإنسان عندما يتذكر يوم القيامة ويشاهد أنه لا ينفعه

THALABI:v10p202/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p202/r2.claim: On that day a person remembers and wishes he had sent deeds ahead for his afterlife, but remembrance then comes too late.
THALABI:v10p202/r2.anchor: يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى يقول يا ليتني قدمت في حياتي لحياتي في الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r2.claim: The person speaking is the human, who wishes he had sent good deeds and righteous work ahead; the omitted object is understood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r2.anchor: ثم فسر ذكراه بقوله: {يقول} (¬7) يعني الإنسان. {يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} أي: قدمت الخير والعمل الصالح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r3.claim: Life here means the afterlife, where there is no death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1)، (ومقاتل (¬2)) (¬3)، والمفسرون (¬4): لآخرتي التي لا موت فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r4.claim: He says the person recognizes there that the afterlife is truly a long life with no death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p521/r4.anchor: علم والله أنه صادق هناك حياة طويلة لا موت فيها

WAHIDI-QT:89:24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:24/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:24/r1.claim: The life for which the person wishes he had prepared is the next world, where there is no death.
WAHIDI-QT:89:24/r1.anchor: أي للدار الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r5.claim: The person longs to have sent deeds ahead for the afterlife, where there is no death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r5.anchor: { يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي } أي: للدار الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r23.claim: Presenting good deeds beforehand means preparing righteous works; the lām in “for my life” can mean purpose, referring to the afterlife, or time, referring to worldly life.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r23.anchor: Takdimden murad ilerisi için önceden hayırlı ameller yapmaktır. لِحَيَاتِى’de lâm ta‘lîl ve tevkīt içindir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r1.claim: These Resurrection scenes remind people who forgot duties to God and others through pride and love of wealth about life's transience, the terror ahead, deserved punishment, and futile regret.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r1.anchor: benlik iddiasına, mal-mülk sevdasına kapılarak Allah’a ve insanlara karşı sorumluluğunu unutan insana, hayatın geçiciliğini, kıyametin dehşetini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r4.claim: The coming of God or His command and the angels' ranks belong to the unseen, whose nature cannot be specified; believers should believe in the afterlife, accountability, and act accordingly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:21/r4.anchor: Allah’ın veya emrinin gelmesi ve meleklerin saf saf olması gayb âleminden olduğu için bunların mahiyeti hakkında bir şey söylemek mümkün değildir

FARRA:v3p261/r15.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r15.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p261/r15.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent deeds ahead for the afterlife, the life of permanence.
FARRA:v3p261/r15.anchor: وجل: يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي (24) لآخرتي التي فيها الحياة والخلود.

JISHUMI:v10p7410/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r18.claim: On that day people remember their evil deeds, neglect of duties, and wasted time, regret their choices, and wish they had worked to ransom themselves.
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r18.anchor: يتذكر الإنسان أفعاله القبيحة، وتركه الواجبات، واشتغاله بما لا ينفعه تندما

JISHUMI:v10p7410/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r20.claim: “I wish I had prepared for my life” means either doing useful good works now for the enduring afterlife or preparing for life after death.
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r20.anchor: ليتني قدمت للحياة الباقية عملا صالحا ينفعني اليوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r3.claim: The threat recalls people's regret for what they neglected when regret can no longer help.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r3.anchor: ثم أتي بالوعيد وذكر تحسرهم على ما فرطوا فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r10.claim: “I sent ahead for my life” can mean the afterlife or one's time alive in this world; the former is clearer and implies human choice, not compulsion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754#2/r10.anchor: هذه ، وهي حياة الآخرة ، أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r1.claim: One reading contrasts the temporary life in which the person could act with the everlasting afterlife for which he should have prepared.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r1.anchor: في الدنيا التي كانت حياتي فيها منقطعة ، لحياتي هذه التي هي دائمة غير منقطعة

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r2.claim: The afterlife is the true life, as 29:64 says; the person wishes he had prepared for it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r2.anchor: وإنما قال : { لحياتى } ولم يقل : لهذه الحياة على معنى أن الحياة كأنها ليست إلا الحياة في الدار الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r3.claim: A second reading says he wishes he had prepared an act that would save him from Hell and restore true life.

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r4.claim: Razi links the absence of life in Hell to 14:17, 20:74, and 87:11–13.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r4.anchor: جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى } ( طه : 74 ) وقال : { ويتجنبها الاشقى * الذى * يصلى النار الكبرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r5.claim: A third reading takes the phrase to mean that he wishes he had acted during his lifetime in this world.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r5.anchor: أن يكون المعنى : فياليتني قدمت وقت حياتي في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r6.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that people freely chose their actions and were not prevented from obedience or compelled into sin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r6.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم ومعلقا بقصدهم وإرادتهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r7.claim: Razi argues that if each intention depends on another intention, this regress is infinite; if it depends on God's intention, the Muʿtazilite claim fails.
RAZI-FULL:v31p159#2/r7.anchor: فقصدهم إن كان معلقا بقصد آخر لزم التسلسل ، وإن كان معلقا بقصد الله فقد بطل الاعتزال

TAB-FULL:v24p391/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r1.claim: The person regrets failing to prepare righteous deeds in worldly life for the everlasting life after death, seeking salvation from God's anger and His good pleasure.
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r1.anchor: في الدنيا من صالح الأعمال لحياتي هذه، التي لا موت بعدها، ما ينجيني من غضب الله

TAB-FULL:v24p391/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God knows the speaker is truthful: the afterlife is a long life with no death.
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} [الفجر: 24] قال: علم الله أنه صادق

TAB-FULL:v24p391/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r3.claim: Qatāda calls the afterlife the long life hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} [الفجر: 24] هناكم والله الحياة الطويلة

TAB-FULL:v24p391/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses the life as the Hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v24p391/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} [الفجر: 24] قال: الآخرة

TABRISI:89:29-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29-30/r1.claim: The wrongdoer wishes he had sent good deeds ahead for his life after death, the enduring life with no death.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r1.anchor: يتمنى أن يكون قد كان عمل الطاعات والحسنات لحياته بعد موته

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r14.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r14.claim: The majority say the regretful person gains no benefit from remembrance then; if he had heeded in earthly life it would have helped him in the next life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r14.anchor: أي منفعة الذكرى، لأنه وقت لا ينفع فيه التذكر، لو اتعظ في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and others take “my life” to mean earthly life; another group says it means the grave life they had denied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r15.anchor: قال الزمخشري وغيره: أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا، كما تقول: جئت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that regret proves people had the choice to obey and were not compelled; Abū Ḥayyān identifies this as Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r16.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهذا أبين دليل على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم

BURHAN:v4p341/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p341/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p341/r1.claim: Lām can mean in or within, as in the scales set up for the Day of Resurrection and wishing one had sent ahead for one’s life.

ITQAN:v2p497/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.claim: Lām can mean 'in' for the Day of Resurrection or its appointed time; 'for my life' may mean during my life or, alternatively, for the sake of the afterlife.
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.anchor: أي في حياتي وقيل هي فيها للتعليل أي لأجل حياتي في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r1.speaker: الزمخشري وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and others take “for my life” as life in this world, as in expressions tied to sunrise or a date.
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري وغيره : أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا ، كما تقول : جئت لطلوع الشمس ولتاريخ كذا وكذا .

ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r2.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r2.claim: Another group understands it as “for my life in my grave,” the life they had denied.
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r2.anchor: وقال قوم : لحياتي في قبري ، يعني الذي كنت أكذب به .

ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that remorse proves people had choice and intention rather than being compelled to obey or sin; the author says this is the Muʿtazilī approach.
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري : وهذا أبين دليل على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم ومعلقاً بقصدهم وإرادتهم ، وأنهم لم يكونوا محجورين عن الطاعات مجبرين على المعاصي

ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:24/r4.claim: The author identifies al-Zamakhsharī’s inference from remorse to free choice as following the Muʿtazilī doctrine.

ALUSI:89:24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:24/r1.claim: The clause may replace by inclusion the earlier remembrance clause, or stand independently as an answer to the implied question of what the person says when remembering.
ALUSI:89:24/r1.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال نشأ منه كأنه قيل ماذا يقول عند تذكره

ALUSI:89:24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:24/r2.claim: On the preferred causal reading, the lām means for the sake of my afterlife; the omitted object is good deeds that would benefit him there.
ALUSI:89:24/r2.anchor: واللام للتعليل والمراد بحياته حياته في الآخرة ومفعول قدمت محذوف

ALUSI:89:24/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:89:24/r3.claim: A reported causal reading instead takes the wish as seeking a beneficial life because he then neither dies nor lives; al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI:89:24/r3.anchor: وقيل اللام للتعليل إلا أن المعنى بيا ليتني قدمت أعمالا صالحة لأجل أن أحيا حياة نافعة

ALUSI:89:24/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:24/r4.claim: The lām may mark time, as in writing for a date or coming at sunrise; life then means worldly life, when good deeds could have been done to benefit him now.
ALUSI:89:24/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون اللام توقيتية مثلها في نحو كتبته لخمس عشرة ليلة

ALUSI:89:24/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:24/r5.claim: The wish implies only that the person believed he could present good deeds; it does not prove independent human agency, since ability may be God's alone or created by God when directing acquired capacity.
ALUSI:89:24/r5.anchor: وليس في هذا التمني شائبة دلالة على استقلال العبد بفعله وإنما يدل على اعتقاد كونه متمكنا

ALUSI:89:24/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:89:24/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the wish as evidence for human independence and uses it to answer the determinists, reasoning that a wish conflicts with compulsion.
ALUSI:89:24/r6.anchor: وزعمه الزمخشري دليلا على الاستقلال ورد به على المجبرة

ALUSI:89:24/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:24/r7.speaker: أهل الحق
ALUSI:89:24/r7.claim: Al-Kashf observes that wishes can concern what is already unattainable, as with a drowning person; the people of truth nevertheless do not deny human choice altogether.
ALUSI:89:24/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف إن التمني قد يقع على المتحسيل على أنه حالتئذ كالغريق هذا وأهل الحق لا يقولون بسلب الاختيار بالكلية

BAGHAWI:89:24/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:24/r1.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent good deeds ahead for his afterlife, the life in which there is no death.
BAGHAWI:89:24/r1.anchor: أي قدمت الخير والعمل الصالح لحياتي في الآخرة ،   أي لآخرتي التي لا موت فيها

BAYDAWI:89:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:24/r1.claim: The speaker wishes he had done righteous deeds for this life, or had done them during his worldly life.
BAYDAWI:89:24/r1.anchor: أي لحياتي هذه أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا أعمالا صالحة

BAYDAWI:89:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:24/r2.claim: This regret does not prove that a servant acts independently; someone prevented from something may still wish he could have done it.
BAYDAWI:89:24/r2.anchor: وليس في هذا التمني دلالة على استقلال العبد بفعله

BIQAI:89:24/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:24/r1.claim: At judgment there is no action left to undo the past; the person can only voice regret and continually wish for the impossible.
BIQAI:89:24/r1.anchor: الندم يقتضي أن يعمل الإنسان ما ينافيه

BIQAI:89:24/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:24/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:24/r2.claim: To have sent something ahead means to have performed beneficial work and acted in accordance with it.
BIQAI:89:24/r2.anchor: أوقعت التقديم لما ينفعني من الجد والعمل به

BIQAI:89:24/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:24/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:24/r3.claim: “For my life” can mean the days of earthly life or this enduring life after which there is no death; the wish reflects that obedience was possible in life and only self-diversion kept him from using God's powers for it.
BIQAI:89:24/r3.anchor: أي أيام حياتي في الدنيا أو لأجل حياتي هذه الباقية

DURR:89:24/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:24/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:24/r1.claim: Hasan says that on that day a person knows the warning was true and that the afterlife is a long, deathless life, better than the person's present condition.
DURR:89:24/r1.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه { يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان } إلى قوله : { لحياتي } قال : علم والله أنه صادق هناك حياة طويلة

DURR:89:24/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:24/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:89:24/r2.claim: Mujahid explains 'for my life' as referring to the afterlife.
DURR:89:24/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي } قال : الآخرة

DURR:89:24/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:24/r3.speaker: محمد بن أبي عميرة
DURR:89:24/r3.claim: The Companion Muhammad ibn Abi Umayra says a servant who spent a whole lifetime obeying God would still wish to return to worldly life to gain more reward.
DURR:89:24/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن أبي عميرة رضي الله عنه ، وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:89:24/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r1.claim: The sentence may be spoken aloud in regret, functioning circumstantially with al-insān or as an inclusive substitute for the remembrance clause.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r1.anchor: وجملة : { يقول يا ليتني } الخ يجوز أن يكون قولا باللسان تحسرا وتندما

IBNASHUR:89:24/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may be an inward statement explaining what the person remembers.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله في نفسه فتكون الجملة بيانا لجملة { يتذكر }

IBNASHUR:89:24/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r3.claim: The object of qaddamtu is omitted for concision.

IBNASHUR:89:24/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r4.claim: The lām may mark time: the speaker wishes he had sent deeds ahead during his first life, before death.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r4.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لحياتي } تحتمل معنى التوقيت

IBNASHUR:89:24/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r5.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose: he wishes he had done righteous deeds for complete life free from punishment.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r5.anchor: وتحتمل أن يكون اللام للعلة ، أي قدمت الأعمال الصالحة

IBNASHUR:89:24/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r6.claim: Life in punishment is described as neither truly dying nor living, supporting the sense of full life free from torment.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r6.anchor: لأن حياتهم في العذاب حياة غشاوة وغياب

IBNASHUR:89:24/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:24/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:24/r7.claim: The vocative yā draws attention to the wish and underscores its importance on the day it occurs.
IBNASHUR:89:24/r7.anchor: وحرف النداء في قوله : { يا ليتني } للتنبيه اهتماما بهذا التمني

IBNATIYYA:89:24/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r1.claim: Most interpreters take “for my life” to mean the everlasting life of the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r1.anchor: فقال جمهور المتأولين معناه : { لحياتي } الباقية يريد في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA:89:24/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r2.speaker: قوم من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r2.claim: Some say it means life in the grave when the denier is raised, despite having believed he would not live again.
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r2.anchor: وقال قوم من المتأولين : المعنى { لحياتي } في قبري عند بعثي الذي كنت أكذب به وأعتقد أني لن أعود حياً

IBNATIYYA:89:24/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r3.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r3.claim: Others understand it metaphorically: he wishes he had done righteous deeds to enjoy a good, living existence today.
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : { لحياتي } هنا مجاز ، أي { ليتني قدمت } عملاً صالحاً لأنعم به اليوم وأحيا حياة طيبة

IBNATIYYA:89:24/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r4.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes it as referring to the period of his past worldly life, like saying “I came at sunrise.”
IBNATIYYA:89:24/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين لوقت أو لمدة حياتي الماضية في الدنيا ، وهذا كما تقول جئت لطلوع الشمس

IBNKATHIR:89:24/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r1.claim: The wrongdoer regrets past sins, while even the obedient person wishes he had accumulated more acts of obedience.
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r1.anchor: يعني : يندم على ما كان سلف منه من المعاصي - إن كان عاصيا - ويود لو كان ازداد من الطاعات

IBNKATHIR:89:24/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r2.speaker: محمد بن أبي عميرة
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r2.claim: The Companion Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayra says that even a person devoted to worship from birth to old age would deem it insufficient at the Resurrection and wish to return for more reward.
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن أبي عميرة - وكان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال : لو أن عبدا خر على وجهه

IBNKATHIR:89:24/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r3.claim: A second route through ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd attributes the same report to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR:89:24/r3.anchor: ورواه بحير بن سعد ، عن خالد بن معدان ، عن عتبة بن عبد ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:89:24/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:24/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:89:24/r1.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent good deeds from worldly life ahead for his afterlife.
MAWARDI:89:24/r1.anchor: أحدهما : قدمت من دنياي لحياتي في الآخرة ،   قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI:89:24/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:24/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:89:24/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that he wishes he had used his life to prepare for his return in the afterlife.
MAWARDI:89:24/r2.anchor: الثاني : قدمت من حياتي لمعادي في الآخرة ذكره ابن عباس

NASAFI:89:24/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:24/r1.claim: The person means the lasting afterlife by ‘my life’ and wishes he had sent righteous deeds from this transient life ahead for that enduring life.
NASAFI:89:24/r1.anchor: هذه وهي حياة الآخرة أي يا ليتني قدمت الأعمال الصالحة في الحياة الفانية لحياتي الباقية

QURTUBI:89:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:24/r1.claim: The lām in لحياتي means في, so the phrase can mean in my life.
QURTUBI:89:24/r1.anchor: أي في حياتي . فاللام بمعنى في

QURTUBI:89:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:24/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:89:24/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that the speaker wishes he had sent righteous deeds ahead for the life that never ends.
QURTUBI:89:24/r2.anchor: وقيل : أي قدمت عملا صالحا لحياتي ، أي لحياة لا موت فيها

QURTUBI:89:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:24/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:89:24/r3.claim: Since Hell's inhabitants have no pleasant life, the speaker wishes he had done good to escape the Fire and join those who enjoy a good life.
QURTUBI:89:24/r3.anchor: وقيل : حياة أهل النار ليست هنيئة ، فكأنهم لا حياة لهم . فالمعنى : يا ليتني قدمت من الخير لنجاتي من النار
